newsitem.title: FRANCE: French govt silent on Cr Lyonnais report.
newsitem.headline: French govt silent on Cr Lyonnais report.

text.p: The French finance ministry said on Tuesday it had no comment on a report the European Commission was expecting France to provide information on a new rescue plan for ailing bank Credit Lyonnais later in the day.

Sources at the European Commision in Brussels said the European Union executive had not yet received any written or oral plan from Paris to soften the terms of last year's huge restructuring plan approved by the Commission in July 1995.
But they said information was expected to be transmitted to Brussels later on Tuesday. European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert was due to give a news conference on the issue on Wednesday.
The conditions imposed on the bank under last year's French state rescue threaten to tip it back into loss after it crawled back into profit in 1995.

The government and Credit Lyonnais, bailed out by the state in 1994 and 1995 as a result of a disastrous expansion spree, have been in a race against time to come up with new rescue terms before the bank's half-year results on Thursday.

Echoing earlier reports, Paris daily La Tribune said on Tuesday the plan would involve removing the burden from Credit Lyonnais's accounts of a 119-billion-francs ($23.22 billion) loan by the bank to the state-backed rescue vehicle that took over 130 billion francs of its troubled assets last year.
The newspaper said government and bank representatives were meeting on Tuesday to agree on the final shape of the plan.
A source close to talks said the burden of the loan would be lifted from the bank, whose losses totalled 21 billion francs between 1992 and 1994. "That bit is certain," the source said.
The loan which the government obliged the bank to make at below market rates to make it bear some of the cost of the expansion spree is at the heart of its latest woes.

The bank, which eked out a 13 million franc profit in 1995, has said it will cost it three billions this year to finance the loan which banking analysts said could drive it into a half-year loss of up two billion francs.

The newspaper said with the burden of the loan lifted, the bank might be able to post a first half profit of "several hundred million francs". It said the cost of the new plan would be a maximum 10 billion francs with some three billion of the expense coming this year.
It added losses on sales of Credit Lyonnais assets by the state rescue vehicle known as the Public Body for Financing and Restructuring or EPFR could be between 60 and 70 billion francs.

In return for its approval of the 1995 rescue, the European Commission stipulated the holding company belonging to EPFR, the Consortium de Realisation (CDR), should sell 80 percent of the assets over a five year period.
The CDR posted a loss of 21.3 billion francs in 1995.
Press reports have said the total cost of the bank's expansion spree to French taxpayers could eventually hit 100 billion francs. -- Paris Newsroom +33 1 4221 5452 ($1=5.124 French Franc)
